# Watershed review: native source and editable task handoff

This module adds the completed offline review desk to an existing scientific Workspace and converts an explicitly selected saved queue into native candidates and planned tasks. It preserves the original project and existing plans. It uses the actual `Workspace.import_sources`, `source_file`, `ImplementationStore.create`, `attach_file`, `report`, and `retain_report` APIs.

## Receive the complete desk

```sh
python source_tools/watershed_review/receive_review.py \
  --application /absolute/application \
  --workspace /absolute/workspace \
  --delivery /absolute/Upper_Savannah_Watershed_Review \
  --output /absolute/new-receiving-output
```

Add `--review-project /absolute/Upper_Savannah_Review_Project.json` to receive that saved queue as an editable native plan. An optional `--title` labels the plan and `--as-of YYYY-MM-DD` selects the planning/report date. Otherwise the saved project's actual save date is used. This planning date does not book any field visit.

The plan is keyed to the exact original saved JSON. Repeating the same file intake keeps that original plan and its manual edits. Existing plan revisions are never overwritten. The exact review JSON is attached to its original plan. Candidate areas are retained classified hectares; no modeled-benefit array is populated from review scores. Original questions become planned tasks with unknown durations, zero claimed progress and no invented sampling coordinates, dates, costs or observations. The partner can edit the tasks in the existing implementation workspace.

The original Eighteenmile lake-sample plan remains revision 2, and the original station/collection-event plan remains revision 3.

## Open the exact desk from a restored native project

```python
from model.workspace import Workspace
w = Workspace('/absolute/restored/workspace')
path, source = w.source_file(
    '3066545cc6da2cd39b368017c912c83e60be3491e2d9872175c2cbb3afc6a5a5',
    'upper-savannah-watershed-review-desk-20261013',
)
print(path)
```

Open that returned HTML path in an ordinary browser. All relative companions are materialized in the same native source view. Saved project controls provide independent persistence when browser-local storage is unavailable. The generated plan report is retained beneath `implementation/plans/PLAN_ID/reports/REPORT_ID`, and native `model.implementation_cli` exposes show/edit/export/report operations.

Current owner direction: `opportunities/upstate_forever_2026/CURRENT_OWNER_DIRECTION.md` v2026-10-13.3. This additive internal review workflow travels with the original Ecosystem Sciences workstream.

## Native report display improvement

The same original saved task report was refreshed after fixing table widths and keyboard scrolling. Current formatter source is included in the native archive. The guarded `apply_native_report_layout.py --application ACTUAL_APPLICATION` composes only table markup and CSS with a compatible maintained formatter. Its nine non-presentation report files remain byte-identical; all original plan revisions and the earlier report edition remain retained.

Upper Savannah • Working review edition

Watershed review desk

Choose what to investigate, inspect the original evidence, and hand off an editable review queue. Land-cover classifications: 2023 and 2025. Station context: retained 2026 draft and source records.

Source-linked, editable, offline

This desk organizes analyst review. The weights are editable preferences over retained classification differences, separate from native NDR/SDR model results.
Review settings
Preference weights

Starts with equal preferences. Each criterion uses a fixed 217-watershed reference scale. One transition can affect more than one criterion; scores are not summed hectares.

Display geometry is simplified at 60 m; GeoJSON exports retain every original vertex after EPSG:3857 → EPSG:4326 transformation. Areas in the desk come from the original classified raster, not this display.

Review order

Weight-choice counts show how often a watershed enters the top K across 66 exhaustive preference combinations. Ties share a rank and can expand the shortlist.

RankWatershed / retained contextScoreTop K
of 66		Rank

Method, original editions, and practical use

A transparent review order

  1. Select the whole retained domain, a utility's original focus watersheds, or its deduplicated in-domain upstream union.
  2. Compare absolute hectares or hectares per 1,000 classified hectares. Gross developed gain, forest loss, and wetland loss retain their original values. No loss or gain is substituted by net change.
  3. Positive values receive tied midranks on the full 217-watershed reference; zero gross change receives zero. The displayed preference score is the weighted average of those scales.
  4. The sensitivity grid exhausts all three nonnegative weights that sum to ten: 66 choices in ten-percentage-point steps, including single-criterion endpoints. Rank range and top-K counts describe these choices, not probabilities, uncertainty intervals or model calibration.
  5. The trade-off front contains watersheds not dominated on all three criteria within the current view. Reviewers can override rank, record a question and queue any watershed.

Ranking totals are not investment returns, pollutant loads or project effectiveness. A single classification transition can increase more than one screening criterion. The editable lens makes those preferences visible rather than treating them as independent impacts.

Read the source correctly

Annual classifications compare 2023 with 2025 on the original common raster support. A mapped class difference is not an observed event date or a measured causal effect. Developed classes include open space; developed area is not fractional imperviousness. Forest and woody-wetland groups remain separate.

A station or gauge is joined by its original point location. A local gauge is not automatically representative of the whole watershed or its upstream union. “Neither” refers only to these retained inventories. The 2026 assessment is a draft edition, and listed causes require their own relevant source interpretation.

ARJWS and PRWD are two utilities with four original focus HUC12 watersheds. Their source-based upstream unions are whole watersheds within the retained 217-HUC domain, not engineered intake contributing areas or a South Carolina-only reporting mask.

Keep the original source edition with each saved review. A saved project contains your settings and notes, not a new scientific source selection. Source references below reopen original public material when online.
